Risk call: REFUSE. Do not size this one.

Reasons from the brief:
- Drawdown of 97.7% from the 30-minute high, and a 62% loss in the last 15 minutes with net sell flow of -18.7 SOL. Momentum is broken, and most coins never recover a dip like this.
- Pool depth is only 32.5 SOL. A $20 round trip would eat 1.4-5.1% or more in impact and fees, and exits from a thin pool get worse as sellers pile in.
- Sell-to-buy ratio of 0.883 at launch and 217 sellers against 150 buyers in the last 15 minutes show distribution, not accumulation.
- The launch bot and the 596-second graduation delay are noise I can't weigh against the sell pressure.

If the desk overrides, the most I'd allow is $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, and only if the pool recovers and shows net buying. I don't expect that to happen. Skip.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying AlterLife now is weak. Demand was real at launch: 536 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation, a 0.102 top-5 buyer share, and a low top-3 curve share (0.069), so no obvious single-whale pump. Classification is ORGANIC, not factory, and no airdrop dump was seen.

But the recent flow shows demand has already left. In the last 15 minutes, sells were 66.87 SOL against 48.15 SOL of buys, net outflow of 18.72 SOL, with 217 sellers versus 150 buyers. The sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.883 and the coin is down 97.7% from its 30-minute high and 87% over 30 minutes. Pool depth is only 32.5 SOL, so a $20 round trip would eat 1.4-5.1% before any move, and the bundle share of 12% sits on top of a collapsing book. Nothing in the brief says demand will still be here in 30-60 minutes.

Recommendation: no buy. The best case is a speculative bounce on a dead-cat pattern, which is not the kind of edge this desk should take at $20 tickets against a base rate of roughly -20% per trade.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a late dump by early holders. Drawdown from the 30-minute high is 97.7%, and the last 15 minutes show -$18.7 SOL net flow (sells 66.9 vs buys 48.2) with 217 sellers against 150 buyers, a return of -61.9%. Post-graduation, the sell-to-buy ratio was 0.883 across the first two minutes, and a launch bot was present, so early buyers are already exiting. The curve completer holds 31.4% of supply and bundled wallets hold 12.3%, which means insider distribution can continue. With only 32.5 SOL of pool depth, a $20 round trip would pay roughly 5% in fees and impact, and a bounce would need to be large to clear that. The bot-driven launch and the collapse from peak make this a poor entry; skip.
